rows: Issued to: Damietta Combined Cycle Power Station
Procedure: Weekly inspection of automatic operation (I2-W1)

This document sets out the steps for the weekly inspection of the automatic operation of the fire-water pumps. The fire-water pumps consist of the jockey pump and two pumps, one the main pump, which is the electric pump, and the second the standby pump, which is driven by a diesel engine. The jockey pump maintains the pressure of the fire-water lines stable within the required operating limits, as it operates automatically to make up for leakages in the fire-water lines and then stops automatically when the normal pressure is restored. In the event of a large increase in fire-water consumption, which occurs when one of the fire systems operates, or the fire hydrants are opened, or the water monitors for cooling the diesel tanks are opened, the jockey pump cannot make up for the drop in pressure, which causes the electric pump to start automatically. If the electric pump cannot restore the pressure within a specified time, as a result of an increase in fire-water consumption beyond its capacity, or in the event of loss of its electrical supply, the fire diesel then starts automatically in parallel with the electric pump; in this case both the electric and diesel pumps continue to operate until they are stopped manually. This document was prepared by Eng. Yousry Abdel Halim Abdel Latif, tested by Eng. Wasfy William Nashed – Senior Engineer, Occupational Safety and Health Department – and approved by Eng. Ahmed El-Husseiny Abdullah, General Manager. It was reviewed by Chemist Ahmed El-Sayed Ibrahim and Eng. Soliman Zaki Soliman, General Manager of Quality Assurance and Quality Control, and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed Farag Anan – Head of Damietta Power Station Sector – and Eng. Mohamed Hussein Gomaa, Head of Quality Assurance and Quality Control Sector, East Delta Electricity Production Company.
No special tools are needed during inspection work
Slowly open one of the drain valves on the fire-water lines
Note the drop in the fire-water network pressure
Record the pressure reading at which the jockey pump starts automatically
Close the drain valve that was opened in step (1)
Note the rise in the fire-water network pressure as a result of the jockey pump operating
Record the pressure reading at which the jockey pump stops automatically
